text:
maria: Heads-up — canary p95 for decode jumped ~40% after yesterday's runtime merge (commit abc123). Seen across 3 canary hosts. :warning:
perf-bot: Canary perf job failed: https://ci.redwood/internal/1234 — decode p95 320ms -> 450ms :exclamation:
sam: Reproduced locally with model=redwood-open-7B seq=64 q=8. Ran perf harness and recorded stacks. Quick run: `./bench/decode_bench --model 7B --seq 64 --iters 500 --profile`
```
# top stacks
attn_transpose  34.1%
kv_prefetch     12.4%
matmul_fused    11.9%
scheduler::choose_kernel 9.8%
```
kevin: I suspect the new kernel-selector heuristic that landed yesterday is picking a different attn kernel for short/medium seqs. Plan: git-bisect between v20260401..HEAD using the microbench harness. I'll start the bisect and post results.
lia: Microbench numbers from canary vs baseline:
- baseline (pre-merge): decode p95 = 210ms, kv miss rate ~2%
- post-merge canary: decode p95 = 295ms, kv miss rate ~12%
KV cache evictions correlate with higher memcpy in the trace. Prefetch hit-rate dropped.
kevin: Ran bisect, culprit narrowed to commit abc123 (kernel selector refactor). Quick confirm: run with env `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy` on the canary binary.
maria: Tried that on one host: `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy ./serve --canary --model redwood-open-7B` — p95 went back down to ~220ms. Good signal.
sam: From the profile, most extra time is in `attn_kernel::transpose` and an extra `cudaMemcpy` path introduced by the new kernel path. Looks like ordering changed such that we lose a coalesced copy and increase memcpys for short seqs.
kevin: Proposed remediation: revert the selector diff and open a follow-up to add a short-seq-aware preference for the fused kernel, plus KV cache telemetry to detect hit-rate regressions earlier. `git revert abc123 --no-commit` gives immediate perf improvement in local runs.
perf-bot: Rollout hold placed on canary #4567 by deploy-bot — blocking further rollouts.
lia: I'll open the revert PR now and add a microbench regression test exercising seq=32..128 attention path and a KV-cache metrics assertion (miss rate threshold). PR link: https://git.redwood/revert/789 (WIP).
maria: Thanks. Also add a console alert tied to KV miss-rate deltas so we don't miss this pattern in the next canary.
kevin: After revert + verifying tests, we should consider adding an automatic fallback in the selector: if kv_miss_rate jumps >5% on shortseq, force legacy choice for that workload.
sam: Agreed — I'll draft a small telemetry + fallback patch after the revert lands.
lia: Filed follow-ups: REVERT PR, shortseq test, kv-telemetry, selector-fallback. Will assign owners in the PR description.
maria: Great work everyone. Once revert PR is up and CI microbench passes, remove the hold and re-run canary with added telemetry to confirm stability. :thumbsup:
